findings.excerpt:
traceOfFiniteProjective R (Module.Dual R M) f.dualMap =
      traceOfFiniteProjective R M f
findings.problem: The file's only result is a directional normalizing identity. It rewrites the trace on `Module.Dual R M` of `f.dualMap` to the trace on `M` of `f`. The left side is strictly more complex and the right side is a subterm-level simplification, so the rewrite cannot cycle. The sibling trace lemmas in Basic.lean (`traceOfFiniteProjective_dualTensorHom`, `traceOfFiniteProjective_smulRight`) are both @[simp], but this one is not. In the test client, `ideal_dual_trace_control` has to call it by hand, as `simpa only [LinearMap.dualMap_id] using LinearMap.traceOfFiniteProjective_dualMap R I LinearMap.id`. `scalarProjection_dual_trace_control` passes it as an explicit term. Any goal containing `traceOfFiniteProjective R (Module.Dual R M) f.dualMap` therefore cannot be normalized by `simp`. The lemma also takes `R` and `M` as explicit arguments, so each manual use has to supply them.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the theorem `@[simp]`. Optionally make `R` and `M` implicit (`{R : Type uR} {M : Type uM}`), as they are in the sibling simp lemmas, so that rewriting and term uses do not have to supply them. The test usages would then reduce to `simp [LinearMap.dualMap_id]`, or to `traceOfFiniteProjective_dualMap _` without `R I`. The existing `dualMap_id` simp lemma then composes with this one to turn the trace of `LinearMap.id.dualMap` into the trace of `id`.
findings.benefit: The simp set for `traceOfFiniteProjective` becomes closed under dualization. Downstream goals that mix `traceOfFiniteProjective` and `dualMap` normalize automatically to the trace on `M`. This matches the convention of the neighbouring trace lemmas and removes the manual `simpa only ... using` plumbing in clients.

evidence.excerpt: @[simp] theorem traceOfFiniteProjective_smulRight (φ : Module.Dual R M) (x : M) :

simpa only [LinearMap.dualMap_id] using
    LinearMap.traceOfFiniteProjective_dualMap R I (LinearMap.id : I →ₗ[R] I)
